    Robert Mueller died on Friday at age 81. He became the FBI director just a week before the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, and went on to impose the most significant structural and cultural changes in the history of the bureau, seeking to transform it into a 21st-century intelligence service that could protect both national security and civil liberties. But Mueller may be best remembered for what he did after he left the FBI, and how he became a target of President Trump’s anger. In 2017, the Justice Department named him special counsel, just days after Trump dismissed the FBI director, James Comey. In 2019, a 448-page report from Mueller concluded that Russia had systemically sought to help Trump win the 2016 election, and that the candidate and his campaign encouraged their clandestine assistance.     Former FBI director Robert Mueller dead at 81

    CBC News · YouTube
    Corporation
    Robert S. Mueller III, former FBI director and special counsel in the Trump–Russia investigation, has died at 81. A Vietnam veteran and one of the longest-serving FBI leaders, he reshaped the bureau after 9/11 and later led the high-profile Russia probe, bringing charges against several Trump associates. “With deep sadness, we are sharing the news that Bob passed away” on Friday night, his family said in a statement Saturday. “His family asks that their privacy be respected.” Trump posted on social media after the announcement of Mueller’s death: “Robert Mueller just died. Good, I’m glad he’s dead. He can no longer hurt innocent people!” The FBI did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment. 📷: Getty Images

    Robert Mueller, a career prosecutor who became a central figure in two searing national traumas, first as FBI director in the aftermath of the 9/11 terrorist attacks and later as special counsel investigating ties between President Trump’s campaign and Russia, died Friday. He was 81. Mr. Mueller’s family confirmed his death in a statement Saturday to the Associated Press. Mr. Mueller had been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease in 2021, according to a statement his family shared with the New York Times last year. Mr. Mueller was confirmed as FBI director and reported for duty one week before the al-Qaeda assaults on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. Over the next 12 years, he became the longest-serving leader of the FBI since J. Edgar Hoover.
